text: You've just enjoyed a great meal, feeling satisfied and ready to go. The perfect ending to a pleasant evening.
But then the bill arrives, perhaps with suggested tip percentages already calculated right there on the slip.
You glance at the options, and a subtle pressure builds. Is it just about the service, or something else at play?
It's a clever trick: those pre-calculated percentages aren't just suggestions; they're anchors designed to shift your perception of a 'normal' tip.
This system leverages social cues, making you feel a subtle obligation to conform to the higher-end options, even if you hadn't intended to.
The cost? You often end up paying more than you initially planned, driven by an invisible social script rather than pure gratitude. Now you see it.
